answer_findings.RLPERFORMANCE-1: performance lens, medium: All comment pages for the issue are fetched without a server-side time filter; for issues with long comment histories the number of API round-trips and the volume of data written to disk grow linearly with the total comment count. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "if ! rsc_gh "$sd" "$out" api --paginate --repo "$slug" \"; happens when: Every gh-backend claim attempt calls `_ccgl_race_note_first_v`; the `--paginate` flag causes rsc_gh to fetch every page of issue comments, then jq discards everything older than `since` client-side. An issue with 150 comments forces 5+ round-trips; `since` is computed but never passed to the API.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: only comments potentially within the race-detection window are fetched from GitHub — comments older than the window are excluded at the server before pagination begins.)
answer_findings.RLREDTEAM-1: red-team lens, medium: When the POST response has no parseable `created_at` (jq falls back to epoch 0, so `_CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT=0`), the guard is false and `since` stays 0, so every historical concurrent claim note on the issue is included in the read-back; a past epoch's winner note — which is never deleted on release — has the earliest `created_at` and wins, causing the current legitimate run to return `race_lost: true`. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "(( _CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT > 0 )) && since=$(( _CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT - 4 * gt ))"; happens when: A GitHub API POST-comment response without a valid `created_at` field (partial response, proxy truncation, an rc-2 path whose response body lacks the field) while any past winner note exists on the issue — a condition that is permanent after the first successful claim on any issue.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: when `_CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT` is zero the run either refuses with a backend error or uses a `since` value that provably excludes notes from prior label epochs, and a test asserts the correct behavior when the POST reply carries no `created_at`)
answer_findings.RLCORRECTNESS-1: The correctness lens suspects, and could not confirm: When `_ccgl_race_note_post_v` returns rc 2 (POST succeeded but `jq` fails entirely because `$out` holds non-JSON — e.g. an HTML redirect from a wayward proxy — gh exits 0 yet both `.id` and `.created_at` are unparseable), `_CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT` is left at 0 and `since` is left at 0. `_ccgl_race_note_first_v` then matches every concurrent-claim note ever written on the issue (all epochs), and the first (oldest) one wins arbitration; a surviving note from a previous label epoch would cause the current run to lose to a stale holder, even though ADR-005 §5's known-limit rationale says "the arbitration result is still correct" — that rationale holds only when `created_at` is parseable. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "(( _CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT > 0 )) && since=$(( _CCGL_RACE_NOTE_AT - 4 * gt ))"); what would confirm it: add a mock-gh variant that returns `rc=0` with a non-JSON body for the POST call, run `claim_coordinator_claim` with a pre-existing historical concurrent-claim note in `notes-pages/`, and verify whether the run incorrectly loses to that historical note (i.e. confirm whether `since=0` causes the false loser path).. Run what would confirm it: answer done when it holds and you fixed it, or wrong with what you ran and what it showed.
answer_findings.RLSRE-1: sre lens, medium: When _ccgl_race_note_post_v returns rc 1 (POST definitively failed), and then _ccgl_remove_label also fails, the zbuild:claimed label stays on the issue; no event names the stuck label — the pipeline.claim.skipped event that the engine eventually emits says only "coordinator failed", not that the label is still there and will block the next run. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "_ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" || true"; happens when: A transient GitHub API outage hits both the note POST and the label-removal call in the same claim attempt; the first real API failure is expected, but the label that was successfully added moments before now has no cleanup path and no specific visibility.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: when _ccgl_remove_label fails in the backend_error cleanup paths, an event or a stderr line says the label may still be on the issue and the next run may be blocked — not only that the coordinator failed.); the same kind of problem also at: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | _ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" || true
answer_findings.RLSRE-2: sre lens, low: The DSRACE-7 re-read of the issue after posting the holder record swallows its own failure with || true and no event or stderr line; if the re-read fails, arbitration continues with stale label state and no record of why. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "_ccgl_read_labels "$issue" || true"; happens when: A momentary GitHub API error on the issue-view call that follows the note POST; the run proceeds to arbitration without any log entry that the re-read was skipped.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: a failure of _ccgl_read_labels in the DSRACE-7 re-read path produces at least a stderr line saying the re-read failed and arbitration is proceeding without fresh state.)
answer_findings.RLSRE-3: sre lens, low: When the losing run's PATCH of its concurrent-claim note to "not started" fails, the failure is consumed by || true with no event or stderr line; an operator watching the issue sees the note body remain as "concurrent claim by `<holder>`" with no indication that the update was attempted and failed. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "_ccgl_race_note_update "$note_id" "$_CCGL_SLUG" "$issue" "$winner" || true"; happens when: A transient PATCH failure after the race is settled; the loser has already been refused, so the failure is non-blocking, but the note stays in a misleading state and nothing says why.; fix: code; ACCEPTED IF: a failure of _ccgl_race_note_update produces at least a stderr line naming the note id and winner so an operator can tell whether the "not started" update was lost.)
